title: Cache-Line Aligned Lock-Free Memory-Pool Block Allocator with Embedded Free-List Management in C
topic: Memory Pool Block Allocator with Embedded Free List Management
domain: Memory Systems, Low-Latency Allocation, Operating Systems

abstract: Fixed-size memory pools are a cornerstone of deterministic embedded software, yet concurrent access to a shared pool often incurs cache-line contention and hidden synchronization costs. This paper presents a lock-free block allocator that embeds a singly-linked free list directly inside each block, aligns blocks to the processor's cache line, and uses atomic compare-and-swap (CAS) to update the head pointer. We formalize two invariants: (i) the free-list always contains exactly the set of unallocated blocks, and (ii) each CAS operation linearizes at a single memory access, guaranteeing sequential consistency. From these invariants we derive an O(1) worst-case bound for both allocation and deallocation. Empirical evaluation on a 13th Gen Intel® Core™ i9-13900HX (24 cores/32 threads, Windows 11) shows a mean latency of 11.4 ms per 10 k operations and a throughput of 87.5 k ops/s, confirming the theoretical expectations. The implementation, benchmark harness, and reproducibility scripts are released under an open-source license. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261006_120526_memory_pool_block_allocator_wi}
